title: Histological analysis of invasive glioblastoma organoids embedded in a 3D collagen matrix
protocol: Collect a spheroid with a cut tip in a 0.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Remove the supernatant and let the spheroid in a small residual volume.
Wash the spheroid carefully with 100 μL PBS twice.
Remove the PBS and let the spheroid in a small residual volume.
Pipette 150 μL of collagen matrix with a cut tip.
Resuspend the spheroid in the collagen matrix.
Aspirate the spheroid and the collagen matrix with the same tip.
Place it gently on the permeable support for a 24-well plate with a 0.8 μm transparent PET membrane.
Center the spheroid in the permeable support.
Incubate 30 min at 37°C.
Add 150 μL of NBM in the well.
Incubate 24 hours at 37°C.
Remove the supernatant by inverting the insert.
Fill the insert with 500 μL paraformaldehyde (PFA) 4%.
Incubate 4 hours at 24°C.
Wash the sample with PBS thrice.
Remove PBS by inverting the permeable support.
Fill the insert with 500 μL of ethanol 70% and incubate 1 hour at 24°C.
Remove ethanol 70% by inverting the insert.
Fill the insert with 500 μL of ethanol 70% and incubate 12 hours at 24°C.
Allow the gel to cool down to approximately 37°C–40°C.
Fill the insert with 500 μL of liquid agarose gel.
Flip the permeable insert down, and carefully remove the membrane to demold the sample.
Cut a part of the agarose using a scalpel.
Deposit the sample in a disposable histology mold.
Fill the mold again with non-boiling liquid agarose gel 1%.
Cut the agarose into a small cube.
Gently cut the membrane along the edge of the insert, then remove it from the insert with fine forceps.
Shape a small parallelepiped sample.
Place the sample in embedding cassettes.
Immerse the cassette in ethanol 96% at 24°C for 1 hour.
Repeat step 3 once more.
Immerse the cassette in absolute ethanol at 24°C for 12 hours.
Immerse the cassette in absolute ethanol at 24°C for 1 hour.
Store the sample in absolute ethanol at 4°C for a few days if needed, then repeat an ethanol absolute bath for 1 hour before proceeding to toluene.
Immerse the cassette in toluene at 24°C for 45 minutes.
Repeat step 8 once more.
Immerse the cassette in liquid paraffin at 60°C for 1 hour.
Repeat step 10 once more.
Insert the sample into the desired direction in the inclusion block.
Embed the sample with paraffin.
Store the paraffin-embedded samples at 24°C for long-term storage.
Cut the paraffin block with a microtome to produce thin sections of 10 μm thickness.
Collect the sections on glass slides.
Dry the collected sections.
On a slide covered with water heated to 37°C, place the paraffin section on the hot water to expand.
Remove water from the slide.
Dry them at 37°C for 12–24 h.
Immerse the paraffin-embedded sections in toluene at 24°C for 5 min, twice.
Immerse the paraffin-embedded sections in ethanol at 24°C absolute for 5 min.
Immerse the paraffin-embedded sections in ethanol at 24°C 96% for 5 min.
Immerse the paraffin-embedded sections in ethanol at 24°C 70% for 5 min.
Immerse the paraffin-embedded sections in distilled H2O at 24°C for 5 min.
Immerse the paraffin-embedded sections in citrate buffer at 95°C for 1 h.
Permeabilize the samples with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS for 15 min.
Wash permeabilized samples in PBS for 5 min.
Block the samples with 1% bovine serum albumin and 2% donkey serum in PBS (blocking buffer) for 1 h.
Delineate the section with hydrophobic pen.
Incubate the sections with primary antibodies (1:100) in blocking buffer at 4°C for 12–24 h.
Wash the incubated samples in PBS thrice.
Incubate samples for 1 hour at 24°C in blocking buffer containing secondary antibodies, DAPI, and Phalloidin rhodamine.
Wash samples in PBS three times.
Mount samples with ProLong Gold antifade reagent.
Image samples with a confocal microscope.
